name: rsi_connors_pullback_v42
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY sustains above its 17-minute SMA — confirming institutional order flow is net bullish across the morning session — a sharp 30-second selloff that drives RSI(6) below 15 reflects transient stop-loss hunting by HFT scalpers or retail panic liquidation. On the NIFTY index, VWAP-benchmarked institutional algos and index futures arbitrageurs treat these dips as favorable execution opportunities versus their daily benchmark, injecting coordinated buy flow within 15-45 seconds. NIFTY's index composition (50-stock basket) dampens the idiosyncratic gap risk that afflicts individual Connors setups, making the overshoot predictable and the mean-reversion swift. The mirror applies bearishly: RSI(6) > 85 while below the 17-minute SMA signals an exhaustion rally that short-selling algos fade aggressively.

indicators.name: sma_200
indicators.purpose: Trend context filter. 200 × 5s = 1000s ≈ 17 minutes. This spans the post-open settling window and captures the current intraday directional bias set by institutional order flow. Shorter SMA (e.g., 60 bars = 5 min) flips too readily on microvolatility; longer (720 bars = 1 hr) misses intraday trend reversals. 17 minutes matches the original's 200-bar 5-minute SMA reduced proportionally to the hold-time ratio (90s hold vs 150min original hold ≈ 60x compression, but SMA context is kept at 17 min rather than 2.5 min because it's a regime filter not a trigger).

indicators.name: rsi_6
indicators.purpose: Short-term exhaustion detector. 6 × 5s = 30s. The Connors RSI-2 principle requires extreme short-term depletion of directional momentum. At 5-second bars, RSI(2) = 10s captures single-tick noise and is meaningless. RSI(6) = 30s identifies genuine 30-second momentum reversals — the 5-second analog of Connors' original 2-period reading on 5-minute bars (both represent ~10 minutes of price action relative to the bar period). Threshold at 15 (below original's 14) is slightly looser to account for NIFTY's index smoothing vs individual stocks.

buy_ce.confirmation: Both conditions on same 5-second bar; SMA must be valid (bar > 200)

conditions: rsi_6 > rsi_high (default 85: extreme 30-second overbought reading — failed rally)
buy_pe.confirmation: Both conditions on same 5-second bar; SMA must be valid (bar > 200)

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts ≈ 6 spot pts. NIFTY RSI(6) < 15 oversold bounces should kick in within the first 6 spot points of continuation. If the index drops a further 6 spot pts (option goes 3 pts against us), the trend-context filter has failed — institutional buyers are not showing up and the pullback is a genuine reversal. Calibrated against 30-second typical NIFTY option moves of 2-5 pts; stop sits at 3 to allow 1 bar of noise but exit before full downleg.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts ≈ 10 spot pts. First-leg Connors bounce on NIFTY recovers to the short-period MA within 45-90 seconds. A 30-second oversold spike on NIFTY typically reverts 10-15 spot points as the institutional algos re-accumulate. Targeting 5 option pts captures the lower bound of this reversion (1:1.67 R:R), consistent with typical 1-minute NIFTY option moves of 3-7 pts.

filters.vix_filter: none (VIX not used — RSI extremes already incorporate volatility regime)
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; skip first 5 minutes of session (pre-open noise)
filters.volume_filter: none (NIFTY index volume is noisy; SMA trend filter is sufficient)
filters.trend_filter: SMA(200) on spot close provides the trend regime gate
filters.spread_filter: none (limit order execution, no bid-ask spread cost)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — RSI exhaustion signals are simple and widely known; edge depends on NIFTY's specific institutional structure providing reliable 30-90 second mean reversion

adaptation_notes: Original strategy applies Connors RSI-2 to individual nifty50 stocks (5-min bars, 150-300 min hold). Key adaptations: (1) Universe collapsed from stock basket to NIFTY index directly — the thesis (RSI exhaustion + trend context) applies more cleanly to the index where institutional flow is dominant and idiosyncratic gaps are absent. (2) RSI period changed from 2 (5-min bars = 10 min of data) to 6 (5-second bars = 30 sec of data) — the Connors principle is about EXTREME short-term exhaustion; 30s on the index preserves that spirit while filtering sub-10s tick noise. (3) SMA(200) kept at 200 bars but now at 5-second resolution = 17 min rather than 1000 min — this is the correct time adaptation because 17 min captures the current intraday trend context, which is what the original SMA(200) at 5-min provided for a 150-300 min hold. (4) Hold time compressed from 150-300 min to 15-90 seconds; exit is now time-stop + fixed target rather than 'close > SMA(5)'. (5) Symmetric short side added (rsi_6 > 85 below SMA) — original was long-only; the logic applies symmetrically on an index.
weaknesses: RSI(6) at 5-second resolution fires frequently during trending NIFTY sessions — may produce too many entries without additional momentum confirmation
SMA(200) trend filter takes 17 minutes to initialize, missing early morning setups
Connors RSI-2 is primarily a mean-reversion tool; underperforms in strong breakout sessions where NIFTY trends continuously without RSI reversion
Single-indicator entry (RSI extremes only) is vulnerable to microstructure noise on NIFTY during news events
